q: Prokhorov's theorem characterises relative compactness of families of probability measures on a Polish space (X,d). A family Π of probability measures is relatively compact in the weak topology if and only if it is:
opts: Tight: for every ε > 0, there exists a compact K ⊂ X with μ(K) > 1 − ε for all μ ∈ Π
Supported on a common compact set
exp: Prokhorov's theorem: on a Polish space, weak relative compactness ↔ tightness. Tightness means the probability mass can be concentrated in compact sets uniformly. This is the main tool for proving existence of weak limits of sequences of probability measures (e.g., invariant measures of dynamical systems).
